sentences.text: This predator measured approximately 6 meters in length and weighed about 700 kilograms.
Despite numerous bone discoveries, no complete skeleton of Megalosaurus has ever been found.
The upper jaw bone, known as the maxilla, bears thirteen teeth.
A broken neck vertebra from the New Park Quarry reveals large internal air chambers and heavy pneumatization with large pleurocoels on its sides.
The only known ulna specimen is 232 millimeters long with a minimal shaft circumference of 142 millimeters.
Buckland's 1824 description estimated Megalosaurus at 40 feet long and weighing as much as a seven-foot-tall elephant.
Replicas of the Ardley footprints are displayed on the lawn of the Oxford University Museum of Natural History.
In 1852, Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins was commissioned to build a Megalosaurus model for the Crystal Palace exhibition, which is still preserved today.
The genus Megalosaurus was first described by William Buckland in 1824.
A fragment of a Megalosaurus bone was recovered from Stonesfield limestone quarry in Oxfordshire in 1676.
Remains from the early Bathonian Chipping Norton Limestone Formation were referred to Megalosaurus in 1939.
Researcher Benson concluded in 2010 that Megalosaurus was the apex predator of its habitat based on its size and distribution.
Megalosaurus may have hunted stegosaurs and sauropods.
Although Megalosaurus was a large carnivore capable of attacking large sauropods, it likely obtained some food through scavenging.
A rib described by Sir Richard Owen shows a pathological swelling caused by a healed fracture at the joint where it connected to the spine.
One of the Ardley tracks shows a theropod accelerating from walking to running.
Today, only M. bucklandii is considered a true Megalosaurus species, as other species assigned to the genus are not directly related to it.
William Buckland classified Megalosaurus as a giant animal belonging to the Sauria, a group of lizards that at the time included crocodiles.
Owen listed Megalosaurus as one of three examples of higher-level reptiles alongside Iguanodon and Hylaeosaurus.
For decades after its discovery, researchers considered Megalosaurus the definitive or typical large carnivorous dinosaur.
Megalosaurus lived approximately 166 million years ago during the Middle Jurassic Bathonian age.
Megalosaurus lived in Europe during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 166 to 168 million years ago.
The existence of Megalosaurus challenged Christian orthodoxy regarding the origin of suffering and death.
It is debated whether Stonesfield material represents a single taxon.
Researchers suggest the Stonesfield Slate fossils, associated with Megalosaurus, may belong to several possibly unrelated theropod species.
Some researchers argue that Megalosaurus is a nomen dubium because they could not find characteristics to distinguish it from its relatives.
Researchers suggest that Megalosaurus valens likely represents fossil material of Allosaurus.
